name: COLOMBIA

flag.title: Tricolor Patria
flag.note: Yellow, blue & red — bold equal stripes

lead: Colombia is at the top of South America. The Andes split into three ranges here, then melt into Amazon jungle and Caribbean beaches. It is the only South American country with coasts on both the Pacific and the Caribbean. It has more bird species than any other country.
geo: Three Andes ranges run from top to bottom. Bogotá is so high that visitors feel dizzy walking. Cowboys herd cattle on the grasslands of Los Llanos.
The Amazon rainforest begins in the south. The north has golden beaches and coral reefs. San Andrés island belongs to Colombia. It lies closer to Nicaragua than to Bogotá.
animals: Colombia has over 1,900 bird species, a world record. The national bird is the Andean condor. The Andean cock-of-the-rock looks like it wears an orange crash helmet.
Spectacled bears, South America's only bears, roam the cloud forests. Pink river dolphins swim in Amazon rivers. Poison dart frogs, no bigger than a thumbnail, glow blue and red to warn predators.
culture: Music is everywhere in Colombia. Cumbia rhythms pound in coastal towns. The Barranquilla Carnival lasts four days. UNESCO lists it, and only Rio's carnival is bigger.
Farmers grow coffee on steep, misty hillsides. People sip small, strong cups called tinto all day. Every August, Medellín's Feria de las Flores fills the city with flowers.
history: Long before Europeans came, the Muisca people traded emeralds on Bogotá's high plateau. Spanish conquistadors arrived in the 1500s, drawn by legends of El Dorado.
Simón Bolívar led the fight for independence, and Colombia broke free in 1819. A 2016 peace deal ended the world's longest guerrilla war.
wows: Colombia exports 200,000 tonnes of cut flowers a year, second only to the Netherlands.
Bogotá's TransMilenio buses carry 2.4 million people daily.
The Lost City is 650 years older than Machu Picchu.
Colombia produces about 15% of the world's finest emeralds.
Colombia has 59 national parks covering 12% of its land.
Medellín won the world's most innovative city award in 2013.
Colombia's Pacific coast gets up to 13,000 mm of rain a year.

myths.fact: They are seeds. Each one sits inside a red fruit called a coffee cherry.
Piranhas mostly eat fish, insects and plants. Attacks on people are very rare.
